name: escape-evil-ghostel
comment: Insert-state ESC routing in evil-ghostel (evil-ghostel-escape / C-c C-r / C-c <escape>). The terminal program is the oracle: `altkey TAG` (a zsh function) enters the alternate screen, reads one raw key and prints GOT-TAG-<byte> (27 = ESC reached the app, none = nothing arrived within the timeout), so each group asserts both the evil state and what the program actually received. Covers auto/terminal/evil on the main and alternate screen, the C-c C-r toggle and numeric prefixes, the option's effect on new buffers, C-c <escape>, and the alt-screen stand-down of the prompt remaps (G, j) with a main-screen control. Every group resets the routing to auto and starts from insert state at an empty prompt; each uses unique marker text. Driven on zsh.

eval: (defun eg-esc--want (tag state mode) (unless (and (eq evil-state state) (eq evil-ghostel--escape-mode mode)) (error "%s: want state=%s mode=%s, got state=%s mode=%s alt=%s" tag state mode evil-state evil-ghostel--escape-mode (ghostel-alt-screen-p))))
(defun eg-esc--alt (tag want) (unless (eq (and (ghostel-alt-screen-p) t) want) (error "%s: alt-screen=%s, want %s" tag (ghostel-alt-screen-p) want)))

steps.comment: short prompt; altkey TAG [SECS] enters the alternate screen, mainkey TAG [SECS] stays on the main screen; both read one raw key (SECS timeout) and print GOT-TAG-<byte value or none>, the oracle for what ESC delivered

steps.type: altkey() { printf '\e[?1049h\e[2J\e[H%s' "ALT-$1"; local k v; read -rsk1 -t ${2:-3} k; [[ -z $k ]] && v=none || v=$((#k)); printf '\e[?1049l'; echo "GOT-$1-$v"; }
mainkey() { local k v; read -rsk1 -t ${2:-3} k; [[ -z $k ]] && v=none || v=$((#k)); echo "GOT-$1-$v"; }

steps.comment: main screen, auto: ESC switches to normal state and nothing reaches the program
alt screen, auto: ESC reaches the app (byte 27) and the state stays insert; once the app has left, ESC is evil's again

steps.eval: (unless evil-ghostel--escape-hint-shown (error "ALT-AUTO-HINT one-time hint flag not set after first alt-screen ESC"))

steps.comment: C-c C-r in the alt-screen app: auto -> evil; ESC then goes to evil (normal state) and the app receives nothing
C-c C-r again (evil -> auto) inside the app: ESC reaches the app again
C-c C-r on the main screen from auto: terminal; the program receives ESC (27) and the state stays insert; a second C-c C-r returns to auto
explicit terminal mode in an alt-screen app: ESC reaches the app, state stays insert
explicit evil mode on the main screen: ESC switches to normal state, nothing reaches the program
numeric prefixes 1/2/3 select auto/terminal/evil directly; an invalid prefix signals a user-error and leaves the mode alone

steps.eval: (let ((r (condition-case e (let ((current-prefix-arg 4)) (call-interactively 'evil-ghostel-toggle-send-escape) 'no-error) (user-error 'user-error) (error (list 'other-error e))))) (unless (eq r 'user-error) (error "PREFIX-INVALID 4 -> %S (mode now %s), want user-error" r evil-ghostel--escape-mode)))

(let ((r (condition-case e (let ((current-prefix-arg 7)) (call-interactively 'evil-ghostel-toggle-send-escape) 'no-error) (user-error 'user-error) (error (list 'other-error e))))) (unless (eq r 'user-error) (error "PREFIX-INVALID 7 -> %S (mode now %s), want user-error" r evil-ghostel--escape-mode)))

(let ((r (condition-case e (let ((current-prefix-arg 0)) (call-interactively 'evil-ghostel-toggle-send-escape) 'no-error) (user-error 'user-error) (error (list 'other-error e))))) (unless (eq r 'user-error) (error "PREFIX-INVALID 0 -> %S (mode now %s), want user-error" r evil-ghostel--escape-mode)))

(let ((r (condition-case e (let ((current-prefix-arg -1)) (call-interactively 'evil-ghostel-toggle-send-escape) 'no-error) (user-error 'user-error) (error (list 'other-error e))))) (unless (eq r 'user-error) (error "PREFIX-INVALID -1 -> %S (mode now %s), want user-error" r evil-ghostel--escape-mode)))

steps.comment: the evil-ghostel-escape option sets the routing of a newly created ghostel buffer; the first buffer keeps its own mode

steps.eval: (unless (eq evil-ghostel--escape-mode 'auto) (error "OPTION-ORIGINAL first buffer mode changed to %s" evil-ghostel--escape-mode))

steps.comment: C-c <escape> forces normal state once without changing the routing: alt-screen app in auto, then main screen in terminal mode; the program receives nothing
normal state inside an alt-screen app: the prompt-specific G and j remaps stand down to plain evil-goto-line / evil-next-line (j unclamped, G reaches the last row, not the cursor row)

steps.eval: (unless (= (line-number-at-pos) (+ eg-esc--row 5)) (error "STANDDOWN-J 5j from row %d (cursor row %d) landed on row %d, want %d" eg-esc--row eg-esc--crow (line-number-at-pos) (+ eg-esc--row 5)))
(unless (= (line-number-at-pos) (line-number-at-pos (point-max))) (error "STANDDOWN-G row %d, last row %d, cursor row %d" (line-number-at-pos) (line-number-at-pos (point-max)) eg-esc--crow))

steps.comment: control for alt-standdown: on the main screen in normal state G is the prompt-aware jump and lands on the live cursor

steps.eval: (unless (= (line-number-at-pos) (line-number-at-pos ghostel--cursor-char-pos)) (error "CONTROL-G point %d row %d, cursor %d row %d" (point) (line-number-at-pos) ghostel--cursor-char-pos (line-number-at-pos ghostel--cursor-char-pos)))
